results.reason: Asks whether to build a requested integration before writing code, matching the go/no-go challenge remit.
Explicitly asks to simplify an over-engineered component without losing behavior.
Directly requests acceptance criteria before implementation.
Asks for a review of a pull request diff touching tenant scoping and a migration.
Intermittent production failures under load call for root-cause diagnosis.
Splitting a large service into modules without behavior change is exactly behavior-preserving restructuring.
Asks how to test a flow with limited time, which is test planning by risk.
Auditing upload and admin endpoints before internet exposure is a security review.
Concrete slow page and API latency targets require measurement-driven optimization.
Zero-downtime column rename on a huge live table is the core migration-safety case.
Designing partner endpoints, errors, pagination, and versioning is API contract design.
Explicitly targets generic AI-generated landing page patterns and filler copy.
Rewriting an error message so users know what to do next matches clear technical prose.
Splitting a mixed branch into reviewable commits and writing the PR is pr-craft.
WCAG failures in keyboard, label, and focus are a direct accessibility audit.
Consolidating button variants and raw hex values into a design system is the stated purpose.
Janky modal motion and gratuitous hover scale are motion quality decisions.
Logs, metrics, traces, and alerts for a new service before on-call is observability instrumentation.
Asks for a go/no-go with blockers before a risky Friday deploy.
Deciding whether to swap moment for date-fns and auditing the tree is dependency hygiene.
A specific Safari CSS bug fix is not covered by any listed skill's remit.
Optimizing a query that scans millions of rows is measurement-driven performance work.
Bulk test generation is implementation work, while test-strategy produces a prioritized plan rather than tests.
Writing an email validation function with tests is ordinary implementation, not covered by a listed skill.
Adding structured logging and a dashboard to a service is exactly observability instrumentation.
Renaming one local variable is too trivial for refactor-safely, which targets structural, behavior-preserving changes.
Raising a timeout to mask flakiness is a symptom patch, not test planning or root-cause work.
A GDPR cookie consent banner is compliance UI work, not security review of auth or exploitable flaws.
Cutting cloud cost is not performance engineering, which is about making software faster.
Writing a reporting SQL query is not a schema or data migration.
Calling the Stripe API to create a charge is API consumption, not API contract design.
Translating a README is translation, not the slop removal or rewriting work described.
Summarizing a PDF is extraction and condensation, not technical writing for a reader's next action.
Resolving a merge conflict in package.json is a mechanics task, not shaping commits and PRs.
Enlarging and repositioning a logo is visual styling, not accessibility auditing.
Choosing a brand palette and logo direction is brand design, not design-system token discipline.
Building a CSS-only spinner is implementation; motion-quality governs motion design decisions, not spinner authoring.
A CI pipeline for running tests is build tooling, not logging, metrics, tracing, or alerting.
A changelog for past releases is effectively release notes, which clear-writing explicitly covers.
Upgrading the runtime version is not package dependency selection, licensing, or bundle-cost hygiene.
